extracted.intended_audience: federal agency EEO officers, HR professionals, agency legal counsel, and agency administrators responsible for affirmative action plans and processing EEO complaints
extracted.subtask_description: Regulatory requirements for federal agencies' disability affirmative action Plans (accessibility, accommodations, utilization analysis, goals, recordkeeping, reporting, Commission review) and procedural rules for class complaints, negotiated-grievance elections, and mixed-case complaints/appeals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notification of basis for denial of reasonable accommodation
rubrics_metrics.description: The Plan shall require the agency to provide a job applicant or employee who is denied a reasonable accommodation with a written notice at the time of the denial, in an accessible format when requested.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notice must: (A) explain reasons for denial and notify of any available internal appeal or informal dispute resolution processes; (B) inform of the right to challenge the denial by filing a complaint under this part; (C) provide instructions on how to file such a complaint; and (D) explain that, pursuant to 29 CFR 1614.105, the right to file a complaint will be lost unless the applicant/employee initiates contact with an EEO Counselor within 45 days of the denial.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accessibility notice for facilities and technology
rubrics_metrics.description: The Plan shall require the agency to adopt, post on its public Web site, and make available to all employees in written and accessible formats, a notice explaining rights under Section 508 and the Architectural Barriers Act.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notice must: (A) explain rights under Section 508 (29 U.S.C. 794d) and the Architectural Barriers Act (42 U.S.C. 4151–4157); (B) provide contact information for agency employee(s) responsible for physical accessibility and for electronic/information technology accessibility; and (C) provide instructions on how to file complaints alleging violations of those accessibility requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assistance with filing complaints at other agencies
rubrics_metrics.description: If an agency's investigation of a Section 508 or Architectural Barriers Act complaint shows a different entity is responsible, the Plan shall require the agency to inform the complainant where to file a complaint against the other entity, if possible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Obligation to provide personal assistance services
rubrics_metrics.description: The Plan shall require the agency to provide an employee with personal assistance services during work hours and job-related travel in addition to professional services required as reasonable accommodation under part 1630, when certain conditions are met.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Services must be provided if: (A) employee requires services because of a targeted disability; (B) provision, together with other reasonable accommodations, would enable the employee to perform essential functions; and (C) provision would not impose undue hardship on the agency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Personal assistance services must be performed by service providers
rubrics_metrics.description: The Plan shall state that personal assistance services must be performed by a personal assistance service provider.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Plan may permit agencies to require providers to serve more than one individual and may permit providers to perform tasks unrelated to personal assistance only to the extent that doing so does not result in failure to provide required personal assistance services in a timely manner.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on adverse action for need for personal assistance services
rubrics_metrics.description: The Plan shall prohibit the agency from taking adverse actions against job applicants or employees based on their need for, or perceived need for, personal assistance services.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selection of personal assistance service providers
rubrics_metrics.description: When selecting someone who will provide personal assistance services to a single individual, the Plan shall require the agency to give primary consideration to the individual's preferences to the extent permitted by law.

rubrics_metrics.name: Written procedures for personal assistance services requests
rubrics_metrics.description: The Plan shall require the agency to adopt, post on its public Web site, and make available to all job applicants and employees in written and accessible formats, procedures for processing requests for personal assistance services.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An agency may satisfy this by stating that the process for requesting personal assistance services, determining whether such services are required, and the agency's right to deny such requests when provision would pose an undue hardship are the same as for reasonable accommodations (see paragraph (d)(3)(i)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Annual utilization analysis
rubrics_metrics.description: The Plan shall require the agency to perform a workforce analysis annually to determine the percentage of its employees at each grade and salary level who have disabilities and who have targeted disabilities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sources of data for utilization analysis
rubrics_metrics.description: For purposes of the utilization analysis, an employee may be classified as having a disability or targeted disability based on specified sources of data.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Permissible sources include: (A) the individual's self-identification on a form (e.g., OPM Standard Form 256), provided the form states information is confidential, used only for statistics, and voluntary; (B) records relating to appointment under a hiring authority that takes disability into account; and (C) records relating to requests for reasonable accommodation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data accuracy for utilization analysis
rubrics_metrics.description: The Plan shall require the agency to take steps to ensure that data collected for the utilization analysis are accurate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adoption of hiring goals (percentages by pay group)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Plan shall commit the agency to specific workforce composition goals regarding employees with disabilities and targeted disabilities by pay group.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Goals: (A) No less than 12% of employees at GS‑11 level and above (and equivalent non-GS positions) are individuals with disabilities; (B) No less than 12% at GS‑10 and below are individuals with disabilities; (C) No less than 2% at GS‑11 and above are individuals with targeted disabilities; (D) No less than 2% at GS‑10 and below are individuals with targeted disabilities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Progression toward goals (required steps)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Plan shall require the agency to take specific steps reasonably designed to gradually increase the number of persons with disabilities or targeted disabilities until it meets the established goals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples include: (A) increased use of hiring authorities that take disability into account; (B) where permitted, consideration of disability or targeted disability status as a positive factor in hiring, promotion, or assignment; (C) disability-related training and education campaigns for all employees; (D) additional outreach or recruitment; (E) increased efforts to hire and retain individuals who require supported employment (including job coach allowances); (F) adoption of training, mentoring, or internship programs for individuals with disabilities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recordkeeping requirements for Plan compliance
rubrics_metrics.description: The Plan shall require the agency to keep records that it may use to determine whether it is complying with nondiscrimination and affirmative action requirements under Section 501, and to make such records available to the Commission upon request.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: At minimum records must include: (i) number of job applications received from individuals with disabilities and number hired; (ii) same for targeted disabilities; (iii) all rescissions of conditional offers, demotions, terminations resulting from medical exams/inquiries; (iv) all employees hired under Schedule A and dates/grade/probationary status/current grade; (v) number of Schedule A hires converted to career or career-conditional appointments and number terminated prior to conversion; (vi) details about each request for reasonable accommodation including (A) specific accommodation requested, (B) job sought/held (series/grade/agency component), (C) whether needed to apply/perform/enjoy benefits, (D) whether request was granted (including alternative accommodation), (E) identity of deciding official, (F) basis for denial if denied, (G) number of days to process request.

rubrics_metrics.name: Annual reporting to the Commission
rubrics_metrics.description: On an annual basis, each federal agency shall submit to the Commission for approval certain materials at such time and manner as the Commission deems appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submissions must include: (i) a copy of its current Plan; (ii) results of the two most recent workforce analyses showing percentages of employees with disabilities and targeted disabilities in each designated pay group; (iii) number of individuals appointed under Schedule A during the previous year and total number of employees whose employment began by Schedule A appointment; (iv) list of changes made to the Plan since prior submission and explanation for changes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public availability of submissions
rubrics_metrics.description: Each agency shall make the information submitted to the Commission available to the public.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: At minimum by posting a copy of the submission on its public Web site and providing a means for members of the public to request copies of the submission in accessible formats.

rubrics_metrics.name: Commission approval and disapproval standards for Plans
rubrics_metrics.description: The Commission shall approve a Plan if it determines the agency has adopted and implemented a Plan that meets the requirements of paragraph (d); it shall disapprove when an agency has failed to adopt and implement such a Plan as required by 29 U.S.C. 791(b).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failure to achieve a numerical goal alone is not grounds for disapproval unless the Plan fails to require specific steps reasonably designed to achieve the goal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Class definition and class complaint prerequisites
rubrics_metrics.description: Defines 'class' and 'class complaint' and sets prerequisites for class complaints filed on behalf of a group alleging discriminatory agency personnel policy or practice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A class is a group allegedly adversely affected by a personnel policy or practice that discriminates on protected bases. A class complaint must allege: (i) class is so numerous that consolidated complaint impractical; (ii) questions of fact common to class; (iii) claims of the agent are typical of class; (iv) the agent/representative will fairly and adequately protect class interests.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pre-complaint processing for class complaints (counseling and timing)
rubrics_metrics.description: An employee/applicant wishing to file a class complaint must seek counseling in accordance with §1614.105 and may move for class certification at any reasonable point when class implications become apparent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If moving for certification after completing counseling, no additional counseling required. Administrative judge shall deny certification when complainant unduly delayed in moving for certification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Filing and presentation requirements for class complaints
rubrics_metrics.description: A class complaint must be signed by the agent or representative, identify the policy/practice adversely affecting the class and the specific action affecting the class agent, and be filed with the agency not later than 15 days after the agent's receipt of notice of right to file a class complaint.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The complaint shall be processed promptly; parties shall cooperate and proceed without undue delay.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acceptance/dismissal procedures and timelines for class complaints
rubrics_metrics.description: Procedures for initial agency/Commission handling, administrative judge review, dismissal grounds, required extensions, subclassing, and agency final action timeline.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Within 30 days of agency receipt: designate agency rep (not per §1614.102(b)(3)), forward complaint and Counselor's report to Commission. Administrative judge may dismiss under §1614.107 or for failing prerequisites in §1614.204(a)(2). If allegation not in Counselor's report, agent afforded 15 days to explain; lack of specificity affords 15 days to provide details or complaint dismissed. Judge shall extend time limits per §§1614.105(a)(2) and 1614.604. Judge may divide class into subclasses. Judge transmits decision to accept/dismiss to agency and agent; agency must issue final order within 40 days of receipt of hearing record and judge's decision and must notify whether it will implement judge's decision; if agency does not implement, must simultaneously appeal under §1614.403 and append appeal to final order. Dismissal must inform agent of appeal rights and include EEOC Form 573.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notification to class members upon acceptance
rubrics_metrics.description: Within 15 days of notice that the administrative judge has accepted a class complaint (or other reasonable time set by judge), the agency shall notify all class members by reasonable means.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notice must include: (i) name of agency/segment, location, date of acceptance; (ii) description of issues accepted; (iii) explanation of binding nature of final decision/resolution on class members; (iv) name, address, telephone number of class representative.

rubrics_metrics.name: Discovery and evidence development in class complaints
rubrics_metrics.description: The administrative judge shall set a time period (at least 60 days, may extend) for both parties to prepare their cases and is entitled to reasonable development of evidence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evidence may be developed through interrogatories, depositions, requests for admissions, stipulations, or production of documents. Objections permitted where information is irrelevant, overburdensome, repetitious, or privileged. If a party fails without good cause to respond to compelled requests and information is solely in that party's control, judge may: draw adverse inference; consider matters established for opposing party; exclude other evidence offered by non-producing party; recommend decision for opposing party; or take other appropriate actions. Judge may direct investigation by an agency certified by the Commission. Both parties must furnish copies of materials they wish to be examined and other requested materials.

rubrics_metrics.name: Opportunity for resolution and procedures for settlement of class complaints
rubrics_metrics.description: Administrative judge must furnish agent and agency rep copies of materials and provide opportunity to discuss and attempt resolution; class complaint may be resolved by agreement at any time pursuant to specified notice and approval procedures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If resolved, terms must be reduced to writing and signed; notice of resolution given to all class members and the judge in same manner as acceptance notice; notice must state relief, agency grant, and name/address of EEOC administrative judge. Within 30 days any class member may petition judge to vacate resolution if it benefits only class agent or is not fair/adequate/reasonable. If judge vacates, may replace class agent. Decision to vacate must inform of right to appeal to EEOC and include EEOC Form 573. If judge finds resolution fair, it binds all class members.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hearing procedures for class complaints
rubrics_metrics.description: After preparation period, the administrative judge shall set a hearing date, conducted in accordance with 29 CFR 1614.109(a)–(f).

rubrics_metrics.name: Administrative judge decisions for class complaints
rubrics_metrics.description: The administrative judge shall transmit to the agency and class agent a decision including findings, systemic relief for the class, and any individual relief where appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If judge finds no class relief appropriate, judge shall determine whether a finding of individual discrimination is warranted and order appropriate relief.

rubrics_metrics.name: Agency final action timeline and contents for class complaints
rubrics_metrics.description: Within 60 days of receipt of the administrative judge's decision, the agency shall take final action by issuing a final order notifying the class agent whether it will implement the judge's decision and providing appeal and litigation information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Final order must notify of right to appeal to EEOC, right to file a civil action and name of proper defendant and applicable time limits. If agency does not issue a final order within 60 days, the administrative judge's decision becomes the final agency action. Final orders are binding on class members and the agency (subject to subpart D). If final order does not implement judge's decision, agency must simultaneously file an appeal under §1614.403 and append a copy to the final order; attach EEOC Form 573. Where final order requires a notice that appeal may be filed, the notice shall inform that appeals may be filed using the EEOC Public Portal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notification of final agency action to class members
rubrics_metrics.description: The agency shall notify class members of the final action and relief awarded, if any, through the same media used to notify of the class complaint's existence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notice shall include information concerning class members' rights to seek individual relief and procedures to follow; notice to be given within 10 days of transmittal of final action to the agent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Relief for individual class members and procedures to claim it
rubrics_metrics.description: When discrimination is found, agency must eliminate/modify the offending policy/practice and provide individual relief, including attorney's fees, to the agent per §1614.501; procedures exist for other scenarios and for class members to file claims for individual relief.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If no class-wide discrimination but class agent was victim, §1614.501 applies and agency must within 60 days issue acknowledgment of receipt of individual complaints subsumed into class complaint and process under subpart A. If class-wide discrimination found and a class member believes entitled to individual relief, class member may file a written claim with agency head or EEO Director within 30 days of receipt of notification; judge retains jurisdiction to resolve disputed claims; claim must specifically show claimant is class member affected and discriminatory action occurred within the class-wide period. When class-wide discrimination found, there is a presumption of discrimination as to each member; agency must show by clear and convincing evidence a member is not entitled to relief. Administrative judge may hold hearings, and agency or Commission may find class-wide discrimination and order remedial action for policies/practices in existence within 45 days of agent's initial contact with Counselor. Agency shall issue final order on each such claim within 90 days of filing; decisions must include notice of appeal/civil action rights per subpart D and applicable time limits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Election between negotiated grievance procedure and EEO complaint
rubrics_metrics.description: When employed by an agency subject to 5 U.S.C. 7121(d) and covered by a collective bargaining agreement that permits discrimination allegations in a negotiated grievance procedure, an individual must elect to raise the matter either under part 1614 (EEO complaint) or the negotiated grievance procedure, but not both.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Election to proceed under this part is made by filing a written complaint; pre-complaint counseling does not constitute election. Filing a complaint under this part bars later filing a grievance on same matter; filing a grievance first results in dismissal without prejudice of any later complaint and advisement of appeal rights from final grievance decision to the Commission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Processing when no grievance coverage or other negotiated-grievance scenarios
rubrics_metrics.description: If a person is not covered by a collective bargaining agreement permitting discrimination grievances, or is employed by an agency not subject to 5 U.S.C. 7121(d) but covered by a negotiated grievance procedure, the regulations prescribe how allegations shall be processed and when time limits may be held in abeyance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where procedures allow, time limits for processing the complaint and for appeal to the Commission may be held in abeyance during grievance processing if the agency notifies the complainant in writing that the complaint will be held in abeyance pursuant to this section.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition and election rules for mixed case complaints/appeals
rubrics_metrics.description: Defines mixed case complaint (discrimination allegations related to an action appealable to the MSPB) and mixed case appeal; sets election rules that a person may initially file either a mixed case complaint with the agency or an appeal with the MSPB but not both.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agency must inform employees subject to MSPB-appealable actions of their right to file either a mixed case complaint with the agency or an MSPB appeal, and whichever is filed first is considered the election. If MSPB appeal is dismissed for jurisdictional reasons, agency must notify individual of right to contact an EEO counselor within 45 days of that notice and to file an EEO complaint; the MSPB filing date is deemed the date of initial contact with the counselor. If MSPB dismisses for jurisdictional reasons after a timely appeal, agency must reissue notice under §1614.108(f) giving right to elect between a hearing and an immediate final decision.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dismissal and abeyance rules for mixed case complaints
rubrics_metrics.description: Agency may dismiss mixed case complaints for reasons in §1614.107; special rules apply when dismissal is based on prior election of MSPB procedures or when jurisdictional questions exist.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If neither agency nor MSPB judge questions MSPB jurisdiction, agency dismisses under §1614.107(a)(4) and advises complainant to bring allegations to MSPB; dismissal advises right to petition EEOC to review MSPB's final decision on discrimination. If agency or MSPB judge questions MSPB jurisdiction, agency holds complaint in abeyance until MSPB judge rules, notifies complainant, instructs to bring allegation to MSPB, tolls all time limitations during abeyance; agency decision to hold in abeyance is not appealable to EEOC. If MSPB finds it has jurisdiction, agency dismisses; if MSPB finds no jurisdiction, agency recommences processing as non-mixed case EEO complaint.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedural exceptions when agency processes mixed case complaints
rubrics_metrics.description: When a complainant elects to proceed under this part rather than with MSPB, subpart A procedures govern except specific exceptions that must be communicated at acceptance and at final decision.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: At acceptance agency must advise: (i) if final decision not issued within 120 days of filing, complainant may appeal to MSPB or file a civil action (but not both); (ii) if dissatisfied with agency's final decision, complainant may appeal to MSPB (not EEOC) within 30 days of receipt. Upon completion of investigation, notice per §1614.108(f) will advise that a final decision will be issued within 45 days without a hearing. At final decision agency must advise complainant of right to appeal to MSPB within 30 days and right to file civil action as provided at §1614.310(a).

rubrics_metrics.name: Petitions to EEOC from MSPB decisions (mixed case)
rubrics_metrics.description: Individuals who have received a final decision from the MSPB on a mixed case appeal or on the appeal of a final decision on a mixed case complaint may petition EEOC to consider that decision, subject to limitations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EEOC will not accept appeals from MSPB dismissals without prejudice. Method of filing: by certified mail, return receipt requested to the Office of Federal Operations, EEOC.
